title: The AI suggests. The machine decides.
hook: Our AI can suggest anything. It can never authorize its own spending.
thesis: TenantOS separates proposing from authorizing: the model proposes, and a separate kernel layer decides whether the effect is authorized. The concrete example: the model can never approve its own spending or its own side effect, because authorization belongs to the authority layer, not the runtime. This is the post that names the exact boundary where model output stops and permission starts.

verified: Model-proposes / kernel-authorizes rule: an LLM never decides whether its own effect is authorized (TENANTOS-HARVEST-ORDER.md, via SYSTEMS.md section 3).
inferred: Stating the boundary this sharply will land with engineers worried about runaway agents.

approval_gate: Nolan approves every exact post. Silence is not approval.
